Subject: Interest in AWS Marketplace private offer — term/discount questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Cloudify is spinning up an inference-heavy pilot and we want to understand how Redwood supports AWS Marketplace private offers. A couple quick questions from procurement before we escalate to legal:

- Is a 36-month private-offer term on the table? If so, does Redwood offer stepped pricing (e.g., higher initial rate, then lower rates after year one)?
- What buyer approvals does AWS require for a private offer to complete? Our procurement team says sometimes the account owner or a buyer approver at AWS has to sign/accept.
- Any standard PO terms you need (net terms, SOC2, data residency notes)?

Procurement is cc'd on this email (procurement@cloudify.com) and would like a short written summary and a PO template if possible.

Simon

Cloudify Inc.

Subject: Re: Interest in AWS Marketplace private offer — term/discount questions

Hi Simon — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front, then a proposed next step.

- 36-month terms: yes, we can support multi-year private offers. We typically present a 12-month and 36-month option. For 36-months we offer deeper discounts but require finance approval and an initial commitment schedule.
- Stepped pricing: we can structure step-down pricing or flat committed-rate schedules. For stepped pricing we usually add a simple staircase (year 1 X, year 2 Y, year 3 Z) and lock it in the private offer.
- Buyer approvals: AWS Marketplace private offers often require the buyer to accept the private offer from their AWS account console. In practice AWS sometimes needs the account owner or a role with procurement privileges to complete acceptance — we can advise on the exact acceptance flow once we have the buyer's AWS account ID.
- Terms/PO: SOC2 attestation is fine (attached a high-level SOC2 summary). We can accept Net-30 or Net-60 on the enterprise offer; long-term commitments usually require a purchase order + underlying private-offer acceptance.

I've attached our PO template and a short SOC2 summary. If you want, we can do a 30-minute procurement/finance sync tomorrow to go over the two price/term options and map the buyer approval path.

Proposed next step: If procurement shares the name/email of the person who will accept the private offer in AWS (and the AWS Account ID), we can prepare a draft private offer and pricing table for review.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_po_template.xlsx (PO template), SOC2-summary.pdf
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Interest in AWS Marketplace private offer — internal: pricing guardrails and approvals

Internal note — quick guardrails for Ben:

1) Discount bands: for mid-market customers like Cloudify we typically allow up to 25% off list on 12-months without extra approvals, and up to 35-40% on 36-months but that requires sign-off from Finance Director and Revenue Ops. Anything >40% needs CRO approval.

2) Billing cadence: for committed multi-year deals, Finance prefers either annual prepay or quarterly invoiced with a signed PO; Net-60 is acceptable but requires Finance to route via AR and may delay onboarding.

3) AWS private-offer logistics: Vanessa, can you confirm if we need a Partner Central config step to enable co-sell benefits for Cloudify? Also, we should include the AWS private-offer URL in the DocuSign/PO so procurement can correlate the accepted offer with the invoice.

4) Risk items: procurement will ask for SOC2 and proof of data residency. We have the SOC2 summary and the runbook for Private deployments; attach when handing off to legal.

Recommended next actions:
- Ben: ask for AWS account ID and procurement contact (email + phone).
- Ben: propose two tidy options (12-mo flat; 36-mo stepped).
- Vanessa: confirm partner/config steps and whether any AWS approval is needed to trigger co-sell.

-Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Simon / Procurement team — thanks. Based on internal guidance here are two draft options for Cloudify to consider. I can push a formal private offer into AWS once you confirm the account details below.

Option A — 12-month committed private offer- Monthly rate: $9,600 (billed monthly)- Effective discount: 25% off list- Billing: Monthly invoiced, Net-30- Attachments: PO template to route to Finance

Option B — 36-month committed private offer (preferred for unit cost)- Year 1: $10,200/mo- Year 2: $8,500/mo- Year 3: $7,600/mo- Effective blended discount: ~35% over term- Billing: Annual prepay (preferred) or Quarterly invoiced with signed PO- Notes: Requires Finance sign-off on discount; Redwood legal will include the private-offer acceptance instructions in the DocuSign package

We will also need the following to prepare the private offer in AWS Marketplace:
- AWS Account ID (the account that will accept the private offer)
- Procurement contact (name, email) and PO if you plan to prepay or invoice
- Preferred billing cadence (annual prepay / quarterly / monthly)

If the procurement team is available, I'll set a 20-min call this week to finalize details and then we can submit the private offer for acceptance.

Best,
Ben
